rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.02, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the BEST config family (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001) at the BUDGET-PROVEN tv_iterations=120 (NOT iter-4's 160 -- see BUDGET below). ONE KNOB: tv_lr 0.01->0.02 (all else IDENTICAL to the iter-2 BEST: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) = the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) REGRESSED (lambda-up exhausted); iter-4 SSIM 0.926664 hr 0.208547 RMSE 7.825e-4 (tv_iterations 120->160, 1227.4s). KEY RECONCILIATION OF THE PLANNED 160->200 KNOB: iter-4's measured elapsed_s was 1227.4s -- already OVER the 1200s HARD 20-min budget at 160 iters -- and 160 iters lifted hr only +0.0031 over the 120-iter iter-2 (0.205364->0.208547), within noise. So tv_iterations 160->200 is INFEASIBLE (cost model fit on the real iter-2/iter-4 pair: c_step=7.47 s/TV-iter, overhead=31.8s => n=200 lands ~1526s = ~25 min, a ~27% overshoot of the wall -> the 214-slice val pass would be killed / the metric invalidated) AND wrong-headed (the iterations lever is already flattening AND budget-capped). FAILURE MODE OBSERVED: the iterations lever has plateaued (120->160 gave +0.003 hr for +33% compute that blew the wall) -- the recon is NOT meaningfully iterations-limited at the cost the budget allows. iter-4's OWN falsifier named the next probe: 'tv_lr (finer convergence per step)'. HYPOTHESIS: doubling the step size (tv_lr 0.01->0.02) lets each of the budget-safe 120 gradient-descent steps travel ~2x further down the data-term gradient, so the recon reaches a LOWER data-term residual within 120 steps (the same/lower residual the 160-iter run was crawling toward) at ZERO extra compute, lowering val_rmse below 7.825e-4 so hr rises above iter-4's 0.208547 -- the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual. Why lr is the right convergence lever and not more iters: the GD schedule is step = lr/(1+decay*it), so with decay=0.01 the per-step distance shrinks ~2.4x by it=119; raising base lr counteracts that decay and converges the data term in fewer steps -- the budget-free way to test the convergence-vs-ceiling question the iter-4 falsifier left open. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.208547 (no gain, or a regression from GD overshoot/oscillation at the larger step), then (a) if hr drops sharply the step is too big and GD overshoots the TV-regularized minimum, and (b) if hr is merely flat then TV is at its REGULARIZATION CEILING on real Mayo LDCT (~0.924 SSIM / ~0.21 hr): 120 iters at lr=0.01 was already converged, the +0.003 from 160 iters was just residual noise, and BOTH the iterations lever (plateaued + budget-capped) AND the step-size lever are exhausted -- accept ~0.21 hr as the structural classical-TV ceiling on this real LDCT substrate and STOP tuning convergence knobs. BUDGET: tv_lr is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- tv_iterations stays at the budget-proven 120 -> identical ~928s wall (cost model: 31.8 + 120*7.47 = 928s, 77% of the 1200s budget, ~272s margin; even at +10% GPU-contention step-cost variance it lands ~1018s, still comfortably under the wall). This DELIBERATELY reverts the over-budget tv_iterations=160 back to 120: the 20-min budget is HARD with no exceptions (six-box rule 5), and iter-4 at 160 already breached it. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.
